requirements.note: Inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first, title + relative/short date (time today, weekday, then M/D/YY) + preview. The preview is short: it shows only the body's first line, and the chevron narrows it further.

Filters title and body live, and shows a proper 'No Results for …' empty state. But the search field sits in a bottom toolbar and stays hidden behind the keyboard while you type, so you can't see your query.

Title and body edits auto-save and the date updates to 'Today'. But the edited note lands second, below a seed note dated later today (10:13 AM), so it doesn't move to the top. Pressing Return in the title dismisses the keyboard instead of moving to the body, so the rest of what you type is lost.

Compose button opens an editor with the title focused. An empty note is discarded on Back (count stays 90); a note with text is kept (91), but like edits it sorts below the 10:13 AM seed note rather than at the top.

Left swipe shows a Delete action and a full swipe deletes. Pin/Unpin and Delete are in a long-press context menu and in the editor toolbar. There is no leading (right) swipe to pin, and a rightward drag on a row opens the note.
'90 Notes' shown as a subtitle under the large title and under the inline title; it updates on create and delete.
Edits, pins, deletions and new notes all survived relaunch.

bugs: Search field in the bottom toolbar doesn't rise above the keyboard; the query is typed blind behind the keyboard.
Edited or new notes don't go to the top of the list: they sort below a seed note dated later today (10:13 AM).
Return in the title field dismisses the keyboard instead of moving to the body; text typed afterwards is lost.
A horizontal rightward drag on a row opens the note, as if it were a tap.
tells: Rows carry disclosure chevrons, which Notes-style lists don't use, and the chevron takes room from the preview.
No leading swipe action for pin; pinning is only in a long-press menu or the editor.
Editor title is a single-line field that truncates ('Podcast rec…') at the largest text size instead of wrapping.
When the keyboard appears, the editor's date label slides up between the nav bar buttons.
Inline nav bar draws as an opaque bar with a hairline, not the soft scroll-edge effect used elsewhere in iOS 27.
Rows are exposed to accessibility as Links, not buttons or cells: a web-like trait.
No Done/checkmark button to end editing in the note editor.
A.scroll: Slow drags, flings and fling-back all tracked smoothly with no blank rows or pop-in, and scroll position was kept when returning from a note. Rows hidden under the bottom search pill can't be tapped.

requirements.note: Apple Notes-like inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first, title + relative date (time, weekday, date) + a long one-line preview.

System search bar under the large title; filters title and body as you type (a body-only word found the right note), with Cancel and clear buttons. With no matches it shows a blank list (count reads '0 Results') and no empty-state message.

Title and body edit in place with a checkmark Done button and no Save step; the note moves to the top of its section with the current time. Opening and leaving a note without editing doesn't change its date.

Compose button in the bottom toolbar opens an editor with the title focused; Return in the title moves to the body. An empty note is discarded on Back; a real note appears at the top and the count goes to 91.
Leading swipe pins/unpins (full swipe pins), trailing swipe shows Delete with a trash icon (full swipe deletes). The editor also has a More menu.
'90 Notes' centered in the bottom toolbar like Apple Notes; updates on create and delete, and reads 'N Results' while searching.
Title edit, body edit, pin and deletion all survived relaunch.

tells: A search with no matches shows an empty list instead of a 'No Results' view.
When scrolled, the search field stays pinned under the inline title and list text shows through it, which looks a little busy.
A seed note dated later today shows the launch time (8:17 AM) instead of its stored time, so the stored date seems to have been changed.
B.scroll: Feels like a native table: slow drags track exactly, flings decelerate naturally with no blank rows or pop-in, pulling past the top rubber-bands, and scroll position is kept when returning from a note.

why: B does everything in the spec with no bugs found and closely matches Apple Notes: leading/trailing swipe actions, a system search bar, the count in the bottom toolbar, Return moving from title to body, and correct move-to-top. A also covers the features, but its search field hides behind the keyboard, edited and new notes don't reliably reach the top, Return in the title loses typing, and it has more non-native touches (chevrons, no pin swipe, a title that truncates at large text).
